blocking_defects.defect: This is the same shared implementation as treatment A. LeakReviewSupport.ReviewScreen/InspectorMark makes a seal reading 'Certified inspector' scale from 1.4x and fade onto the footage by itself. DrawnDashes outlines the shimmer with no actor, and the 'Follow-up inspection' tag flies along a Bezier curve from the screen to the valve vignette with no carrier. No person, hand, stylus or cursor exists anywhere in the film. In B, the panel-overhead, review-panel and inspector-mark shots enlarge the seal, which makes the absence more prominent. It uses the same grammar and the same amber as the software 'Anomaly' flag (s2) and the point-of-interest ring (s4), so with labels covered the software appears to certify the leak. Sources c7 and c15 permit a generic disclosed certified inspector, and prior registered episodes in this engine draw hands and articulated people. Required correction: author a generic, unnamed, disclosed inspector at the review screen whose own action draws the outline, confirms, and hands off the follow-up, with confirmation styling distinct from the AI amber.

The close (panel-wide-hold, then confirm-hold, then blank-box) re-presses the same actorless seal and draws its amber check, then draws an empty 'AI' box. 'Who decides' is answered only by printed words on a badge, and nobody is pictured deciding. The s5 human must carry into the close.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: The intended chain, reconstructed from the executable code, is identical in substance to A but seen mostly from above. Straight down on a caliche pad, a drone rises off its station and heads for the valves while a Texas card pins the Permian and Austin. A flat tablet seen from above lights a flight map, an amber 'Anomaly' flag rises on a valve, and 'The companies say' hooks on. A letter seen from above takes a 'September 30th, 2025' stamp and an 'Approved' mark. Seen from above, the plan draws over the pad, then a close follows the drone to the valve ring and the infrared inset opens. A 'Certified inspector' seal lands on the footage and a follow-up tag flies to the valve. The letter's protocol title highlights AI once. A separate program tag is marked 'Delayed' for January 22nd, 2027 and gets 'Will propose to rescind' on October 7th. The seal checks beside an empty AI box as the window station closes.
story_review.opening_to_ending: B promises to start with who confirms the leak but starts with the drone, exactly like A. It ends on the same actorless badge and empty AI box. The question of who decides is answered only in printed words. The overhead framing adds wall views rather than a new line of understanding.
story_review.weakest_transition: s4 to s5 (26.4 s): the footage moves from the drone's camera to a review screen where no reviewer exists, so the decisive human handoff is missing. B's overhead first shot at s5 (panel-overhead) emphasizes the empty desk.
